summary: No Cesar-specific signal on trans law, enforcement practice, incidents or institutional conduct was identified in the sources reviewed; Cesar stands under Colombia's national framework, and the national assessment applies in this department.
tangentialFactors:
Reporting on armed-group campaigns against trans people in Colombia names Caquetá and La Guajira, where flyers announcing a social cleansing and kill lists of named individuals have circulated since 2024. Those findings sit at the national level. No equivalent reporting names Cesar.

Reporting on the wave of attacks against LGBTQ+ people in Colombia during 2025 gives no departmental breakdown that reaches Cesar.
localsOnly: Nothing in the sources reviewed describes departmental health services, prison practice, police conduct or protection programmes in Cesar, so no resident-facing finding specific to this department can be stated. Identification, health care, custodial and public-accommodation rules reach residents of Cesar through the national framework, which the Colombia record carries.
outOfScopeNotes:
Two of the sources reviewed state expressly that they contain no information on Cesar. No data from the departmental police, the prosecutor's office in Cesar or the departmental health authority appears in the inventory, so enforcement practice in the department is not sourced.

An activist quoted in reporting on Caquetá said the prosecutor's office does not recognise transfemicide and records the killings of trans women as ordinary cases. Whether that practice holds in Cesar is unresolved.

The source describing gender-marker change and notarial procedure is national in scope and gives no departmental detail; that material is carried by the Colombia record.
